title: Assembling the Context
brief: A coding agent works in a repo with house rules: pnpm not npm, tests with `pnpm test`, never edit files under generated/. Every call sends a 6,000-token prefix (base prompt plus 14 tool schemas) into a 16,000-token window, and the model has never seen the house rules. Build the context stack so that at least 85% of changes follow the rules, the context never overflows, and a task costs $0.25 or less.

Nobody told the model the house rules, so it uses the defaults it saw most in training: npm, edit the file you see.
The window overflowed and the task fell out of it.

goals.label: At least 85% of changes follow the house rules

hints: Look at what the model sees: the 6,000-token prefix, then history that grows by 1,000 to 2,400 tokens a turn. Nothing in it mentions pnpm or generated/.
Three blocks are missing or wasteful: project instructions in the system prompt, a running summary instead of the full history, and a cached stable prefix.
Model: put the AGENTS.md rules in System prompt and turn on Cache stable prefix. Add a Memory node of kind summary wired to the model.
explain: The context is something your harness builds on every call. Put the stable blocks first and cache them, put the rules where the model always sees them, and summarize the history so the task never scrolls out.
